title: IOb-SoC-Linux: An Open-Source, Linux-Capable RISC-V SoC Template for IP Core Development
content: IOb-SoC-Linux is an open-source framework for configuring and generating Linux-capable System-on-Chip (SoC) designs targeting RISC-V processors. Built on the Py2HWSW hardware/software co-design framework, it provides a specialized SoC template that contrasts with bare-metal-focused alternatives, offering a reproducible environment for the design, integration, and testing of Intellectual Property (IP) cores under a full Linux software stack. The primary contribution of IOb-SoC-Linux is an IP Core Linux Driver Development tool that, from a peripheral’s hardware register description, automatically generates a register-access Linux kernel driver, its device tree entry, and associated documentation, keeping these software artifacts synchronized with the hardware as it evolves and removing a recurring source of manual, error-prone integration work. The platform supports the open-source VexRiscv and VexiiRiscv RISC-V processors. Beyond the processor subsystem, it integrates the complete infrastructure required for Linux execution: memory management unit, memory controller, peripheral buses, interrupt controllers, timer, UART interface, storage controllers, and configurable IP peripherals. To improve interoperability and reuse, IOb-SoC-Linux adopts the IP-XACT standard (IEEE 1685) alongside the FuseSoC package manager, enabling standardized metadata descriptions and structured package management for hardware IP blocks. This allows hardware components to be readily discovered, configured, and integrated into both the IOb-SoC-Linux environment and the broader open-source hardware ecosystem. The system is designed for portability across multiple FPGA platforms and its generated RTL synthesizes cleanly through an open-source, ASIC-oriented flow to a gate-level netlist, demonstrating its suitability for both FPGA prototyping and ASIC-oriented RTL synthesis.
